sections.overview: Coloma’s pygmy frog was described from Ecuador’s western Andes; current Amphibian Species of the World lists it as Phyllonastes coloma.
sections.identification: The original description distinguishes it by a bright orange underside and the absence of the dorsal bars and chevrons found in some close frogs.
sections.habitat: The species is known from humid montane forest on the Pacific slopes of Ecuador’s western Cordillera, at roughly 1283–2215 m.
sections.diet: The cited taxonomic and distribution accounts do not establish a species-specific diet.
sections.behavior: The available primary description is based on collected specimens and gives little detail about behavior in the wild.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted do not provide a verified account of its breeding or development.
sections.ecology: Its generic placement has changed: the original paper used Noblella, whereas the 2025 revision and current ASW account use Phyllonastes.
sections.conservation: The accounts consulted do not provide a current population trend for this frog.
